title: Alter Ego
build: Male edition first name prompt, with separately published male/female gameplay overlays

records.c: Load-address entry of the female gameplay object. The MAP1 absolute-load object header names load address $8466, and the object's first three bytes are 4C 91 b3, i.e. JMP $B391. Execution of the gameplay occupant begins here and transfers immediately to the setjmp routine. Inputs: The gameplay object has been loaded at $8466 by the MAP1 preamble. Outputs: Control transferred to $B391. Assumptions: valid only while the female gameplay object is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69. The three bytes are typed as code and labelled here because this is the only entry into the occupant; unlike the male edition the target $B391 lies inside this same overlay, so the whole path stays within the female occupant. Clobbers: None at this instruction. Hardware: None.

Female gameplay occupant. Run the gameplay phase and Life Map interface. Inputs: current stage/save state, loaded resident engine, and canonical MAP media. Outputs: long-lived main loop; no normal VM return is reachable. It loads stage configuration, converts initial_cursor_cell_index to row/column, renders and scrolls the map, moves sprite 0, dispatches selected cells, and enters resume/save/status paths. Assumptions: stage 1-7 and validated MAP directories. Clobbers/state: map cursor, stream state, display work, and progression fields. Hardware: VIC-II sprites/bitmap and CIA input through resident helpers. VM entry $84DC, frame -16, bytecode $84E1-$87C3 (365 decoded operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Dispatch one Life Map cell action. Inputs: +8/+10 identify the cell/slot and packed selector metadata from $81C5. Outputs: status/menu result or the result of run_life_map_turn. Selector 0 is inert, 1 opens LIFE TIME, 5 opens life status, and other validated category selectors are unpacked into side, slot, and action arguments for $8A85. Assumptions: selector low nybble is 0-11. Clobbers: VM expression stack and UI work. Hardware: display/input through callees. VM entry $87C5, frame -4, bytecode $87CA-$881A (38 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Open and position the MAP record stream for the current life stage. Inputs: +8 controls initial/retry behavior; $82BD supplies stage. Outputs: active stream identifier at $CADB and positioned framed-record state, or an error result after the retry prompt. Stage 7 selects MAP27's second section; other stages select their matching MAP source. Assumptions: canonical REL framing. Clobbers: stream/file and temporary filename state. Hardware: IEC/CIA 2 through prepare_map_record_stream. VM entry $881B, frame -37, bytecode $8820-$88A8 (63 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Load and validate the current MAP stage section. Inputs: current stage $82BD and optional fresh-load flag +8. Outputs: age bounds at $803B-$803E, transient stage words at $803F-$8042, persisted 48-byte configuration at $81C5, route count/words at $82BB/$81F7, initial cursor $82DB, terminal scene ID $82F5, and block-span stream offset $82F7. It clamps age to the stage minimum and reports malformed lengths. Clobbers: a 514-byte VM frame and MAP stream cursor. Hardware: IEC through stream readers. VM entry $88A9, frame -514, bytecode $88AE-$89DB (137 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Invalidate the active MAP record stream. Inputs: $CADB active-stream identifier. Outputs: expected record ID invalidated through $5F27 and $CADB cleared to zero; no action when already zero. Clobbers: VM primary and stream state. Hardware: none directly. VM entry $8A72, frame 0, bytecode $8A77-$8A84 (6 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Execute one Life Map turn. Inputs: selected row/column/category and mode in VM arguments, current route/config arrays, state vector, and active MAP stream. Outputs: selected episode executed or terminal/stage result returned. It hit-tests the map, selects a remaining category episode, executes descriptor chains, removes finite choices, advances age by compressed-span allocation, handles terminal cells, and redraws transitions. Assumptions: validated route words and nonempty eligible masks. Clobbers: progression, mask, cursor, descriptor, and UI work state. Hardware: VIC-II, CIA input, and SID-backed randomness through callees. VM entry $8A85, frame -5, bytecode $8A8A-$8CA4 (274 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Finish a life stage and apply its financial transition. Inputs: current stage, cash/debt limbs, reverse_stage_index_8_minus_stage, and post-stage menu state. Outputs: next stage selected (wrapping after 7), acquisitions reset at wrap, a stage-scaled debt payment transferred from cash, debt low limb cleared, and the stage stored in the sign convention expected by the next loader. Menu results dispatch save, resume, continue, or exit paths. Assumptions: base-1000 money limbs and nonzero stage divisor. Clobbers: stage, acquisitions, cash/debt, UI and stream state. Hardware: display/input through callees. VM entry $8CFF, frame -4, bytecode $8D04-$8DCF (96 operations).

Female gameplay occupant. Inline-native gateway for episode selection. JSR $7059 consumes both hardware returns; header bytes encode saved workspace count 0 and VM-stack adjustment -16. Execution begins at $8DD6. There is no encoded target pointer and no fallthrough into the header. Assumptions: Valid only while this overlay is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69; the RAM-resident gateway at $7059 must be present and reached by JSR, with two return addresses on the stack. The two header bytes after the JSR must stay typed as data -- $7059 reads them as {saved-workspace count 0, signed stack adjustment -16} and takes the body as return+4, i.e. $8DD6 -- so nothing may be inserted and there is no fallthrough into the header. Hardware: Touches no hardware: a single JSR into the RAM-resident runtime descriptor gateway at $7059. Inputs: none consumed here — the body reads no register or memory location before handing control to RAM:runtime_descriptor_call_gateway, whose inputs apply unchanged. Outputs: none of its own; RAM:runtime_descriptor_call_gateway consumes the pushed return address and continues at the body that follows the two header bytes, so the observable outputs are those of the routine it introduces. Clobbers: nothing of its own — control leaves at once, so only the callee's clobbers apply.

Female gameplay occupant. Select an eligible episode from one stage slot. Inputs: native frame identifies the slot/config record; $81D5-$81F4 holds remaining masks and selector metadata is at $81C5. Outputs: one eligible bit/episode index. Ordinary categories clear the selected slot bit. Selector 6 excludes bits already in $7FC0-$7FC3 and adds the chosen family bit there. Assumptions: at least one eligible bit. Clobbers: A,X,Y, zero-page/native arithmetic and mask work. Hardware: SID-backed randomness through the resident random helper. Reachable code $8DD6-$8F8D and $90A0-$9121; intervening and trailing bytes through $91CC are compiler tables/data.

Female gameplay occupant. Advance age and finances from a selected scene's allocated compressed span. Inputs: 16-bit span argument, age scale $803F/$8040, stage state, thoughtfulness, salary state word 37, and cash/debt resources. Age output: delta=(span*scale+512)>>10 is added to fractional year $7FC4/$7FC5; overflow advances player age $7F74 and child age $7F8C. Financial output for a salaried character: expense_percent=floor((100-thoughtfulness)/2)+5*(life_stage-2), then cash_delta=round(salary_thousands*elapsed_years*(100-expense_percent)*10); zero salary follows the later-stage resource-loss branch. Side-choice callers divide span by three before entry. Assumptions: stage configuration and state vector are loaded. Clobbers: A, X, Y and native multiword arithmetic workspace. Hardware: none. Physical extent $91D3-$9829.

Execution begins at $9830. There is no encoded target pointer and no fallthrough into the header. Assumptions: Valid only while this overlay is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69; the RAM-resident gateway at $7059 must be present and reached by JSR, with two return addresses on the stack. The two header bytes after the JSR must stay typed as data -- $7059 reads them as {saved-workspace count 4, signed stack adjustment -30} and takes the body as return+4, i.e. $9830 -- so nothing may be inserted and there is no fallthrough into the header. Female gameplay occupant. Return the allocated compressed block span for a scene ID. Inputs: scene ID argument, stage terminal/count metadata, and four-byte block-span-table payload offset $82F7. Outputs: zero for scene zero, the exact directory allocation span for a valid scene, or failure for malformed/exhausted stream state. It walks little-endian spans, accumulates the 32-bit payload cursor, and calls VM $9908 to refill the span window. Assumptions: Entered through the $982A shim, which preserves four workspace bytes, so the $7059 frame must be live with $06/$07 valid and X=0 on entry -- X supplies both the zero result and the zero comparison operand. Frame +9/+10 must hold the scene ID, with 0 and $00FF treated as terminators; the four-byte payload offset at $82F7-$82FA must be current, $30-$33 must be the reserved workspace, and $CC65-$CC68 must be free stream scratch. This overlay must be the active occupant of $8466-$CC69. Clobbers: A,X,Y, zero-page $30-$33 and $CC65-$CC68 stream work. Hardware: IEC only through the refill helper. Physical extent $9830-$9907.

Female gameplay occupant. Refill the scene-span stream with retry handling. Called by native span lookup when its local span window is exhausted. Inputs: 32-bit MAP payload cursor at $CC65-$CC68, current stage/stream state, and work buffers. Outputs: validates/reads the next span window, advances the logical cursor through tell_map_payload_offset, resets dependent decoder state, and returns zero on success; media/record errors are reported and retried after stream invalidation. Clobbers: $CAxx stream/decode work and VM temporaries. Hardware: IEC/CIA 2 through MAP stream helpers. VM entry $9908, frame 0, bytecode $990D-$99BB (71 operations); the byte-identical tail $9992-$99BB remains in ordinary RAM.

Female gameplay occupant. Load and LZW-expand one local descriptor chunk from the active scene block.
Inputs: +8 local chunk index.
Outputs: pointer into $C2A2, or zero on failure.
Assumptions: boundary table $CAE5, compressed base $CAAB and file slot $CADB are valid.
Clobbers/state: VM primary/secondary values, expression stack and frame locals are scratch; $CAAF/$CAD1 cache, $CADD descriptor pointer and LZW workspace.
Hardware: MAP seek/read through custom serial layer.
Entry protocol: JSR $70F8 at $9A14; signed frame adjustment -8; bytecode $9A19-$9AE3 (115 decoded operations); native calls $4C12, $4CA1, $5C37, $A4DB, $A4F1. VM opcode $CF restores the frame and returns.

Hardware: display/input/disk through descriptor interpreter.
Entry protocol: JSR $70F8 at $9B18; signed frame adjustment -4; bytecode $9B1D-$9B94 (58 decoded operations); native calls $9A14, $9BF9, $A3D0. VM opcode $CF restores the frame and returns.

Female gameplay occupant. Evaluate the current ordered phase of five-byte state-range conditions.
Inputs: +8 remaining clause count; +10 current clause pointer.
Outputs: updated pointer after the consumed phase on success; zero on the first failed bounded clause.
Assumptions: records are a state byte plus two signed big-endian inclusive bounds. State $FF is a phase separator: entry evaluation stops there and leaves the suffix for presentation opcode 6; it is not an unconditional state test.
Clobbers/state: VM primary/secondary values, expression stack and frame locals are scratch; reads the state vector at $7F40.
Hardware: none.
Entry protocol: JSR $70F8 at $9B96; signed frame adjustment -4; bytecode $9B9B-$9BF8 (76 decoded operations); native calls none. VM opcode $CF restores the frame and returns.

Female gameplay occupant. Interpret one decompressed interaction descriptor. Input: descriptor pointer at $CADD. It evaluates five-byte signed-big-endian inclusive conditions; executes four-byte effects; collects mixed-radix choices; runs the presentation script; substitutes dynamic text; and selects the next local route/control code. Output: next route or terminal control result. Assumptions: the descriptor obeys the exported grammar. Clobbers/state: VM values, expression stack, frame locals, selected state-vector words, choice/radix work and display buffers. Hardware: SID voice-3 noise for random effects and VIC/CIA through UI helpers. Corpus proof: all 5,802 choice radices are 1..12 and all 103 random-modulo operands are 3, 33 or 99, so the data-driven divisors are nonzero.
Entry protocol: JSR $70F8 at $9BF9; signed frame adjustment -94; bytecode $9BFE-$A057 (662 decoded operations); native calls $4697, $4C12, $6E33, $9B96, $A06D, $A235, $A279. VM opcode $CF restores the frame and returns.

Outputs: selected mixed-radix choice/control result when selection is requested; otherwise the text panel is presented and interpretation continues.
Assumptions: descriptor text indices, choice radices, and packed display metadata are valid.
Clobbers/state: VM primary/secondary values, expression stack and frame locals are scratch; $B568 packed-text work, selection/sprite/screen state.
Hardware: VIC-II/CIA through display/input helpers.
Entry protocol: JSR $70F8 at $A06D; signed frame adjustment -3; bytecode $A072-$A233 (220 decoded operations); native calls $44C5, $475D, $545B, $54BF, $554D, $56FF, $5F30. VM opcode $CF restores the frame and returns.

Female edition-shifted mirror of the male gameplay object entry at RAM $B392. Byte-identical body one address lower. Reached through GAMEPLAY_FEMALE_PHASE::$8466 = 4C 91 B3 (JMP $B391). Publishes the VM frame pointer to $C29A/$C29B, copies the eight-byte frame to $02-$09, re-pushes the recovered return address, and jumps to $84DC. Inputs: A valid VM frame and two bytes of native return on the 6502 stack. Outputs: $C29A/$C29B hold the recovery frame pointer; control transferred to female_gameplay_main_loop at $84DC. Assumptions: Valid only in GAMEPLAY_FEMALE_PHASE. This is the fifth edition-shifted pair, alongside $B407/$B408, $B439/$B43A, $B50B/$B50C and $B528/$B529. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $0E/$0F, $02-$09 and two bytes of 6502 stack. Hardware: None directly.

Female edition-shifted mirror of the male non-local exit at RAM $B3B5, one address lower. Four female call sites emit AC B4 B3. Inputs: VM expression stack with one pushed argument word; $C29A/$C29B written by $B391. Outputs: Argument word in VM primary $0A/$0B; VM registers restored; control resumed at the recovery point. Assumptions: $B391 must have run in this phase. Valid only in GAMEPLAY_FEMALE_PHASE. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0A/$0B, $0E/$0F, $02-$09 and two bytes of 6502 stack. Hardware: None directly.

Female edition-shifted occupant; behavior matches the male helper at $B408.
Arithmetic-right-shift a caller-owned signed 32-bit little-endian value by a caller-owned 32-bit count.
Inputs: X is the zero-page address of the count at X..X+3; Y is the zero-page address of the value at Y..Y+3. The active callers supply nonnegative counts.
Outputs: value shifted in place with sign extension; count decremented to $FFFFFFFF; returns A=0, X=0, Y=1.
Assumptions: both four-byte objects fit in zero page and do not overlap. Counts of 32 or more converge to all sign bits.
Clobbers/state: $02/$03 hold the two base addresses; the count buffer and flags are scratch.
Hardware: none. The routine snapshots the value's sign in carry, decrements the count, rotates high byte to low once per nonnegative count, and stops after the decrement crosses below zero.

Female edition-shifted occupant; behavior matches the male helper at $B43A.
Multiply a caller-owned unsigned 16-bit little-endian value by AX using a 16-round shift/add product.
Inputs: A is factor low, X factor high, and Y is the zero-page address of the value at Y/Y+1.
Outputs: low product word replaces the caller's value; high product word remains in $02/$03; returns A=0, X=0, Y=1.
Assumptions: the two-byte caller value fits in zero page and does not overlap $02/$03 or $24/$25.
Clobbers/state: $02/$03 product high, $24/$25 saved factor, caller value, and flags.
Hardware: none. Each source bit conditionally adds the factor to $02/$03, then ROR propagates through the four-byte accumulator/value pair.

Female edition-shifted occupant; behavior matches the male helper one byte later.
Shift a caller-owned 16-bit little-endian value left by a 16-bit count. Input: A=count low byte, X=count high byte, Y=direct-page address of the value at Y/Y+1. The low count drives the first shift group and each remaining high-count unit performs another 256 ASL/ROL rounds. Output: shifted value in place; A=0, X=0, Y=1. Assumptions: Valid only while the female overlay is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69. Y must be a zero-page address whose 16-bit value occupies Y and Y+1, because the routine transfers Y into X and indexes $00,X/$01,X, so Y must be $FE or below; the shared RAM zero page $02/$03 must be free as the private count. A and X are consumed as the count and returned as zero. Clobbers $02/$03 as the private count and processor flags. Counts greater than 15 naturally shift all source bits out. Hardware: Touches no hardware: zero-page shifting only, on the RAM zero page shared with the male edition. Clobbers: A, X, Y and the processor flags; writes RAM:shared_scratch_02_lo, RAM:shared_scratch_02_hi, $00,X, $01,X.

Female edition-shifted occupant; behavior matches the male helper one byte later.
Arithmetic-right-shift a caller-owned signed 16-bit value by a 16-bit count. Input: A=count low byte, X=count high byte, Y=direct-page address of the value at Y/Y+1. Negative values shift with carry set to preserve the sign bit; nonnegative values share the logical-right-shift loop at $B550. Output: shifted value in place; A=0, X=0, Y=1. Assumptions: Valid only while the female overlay is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69. Y must be a zero-page address holding the 16-bit value at Y and Y+1 (so $FE or below), and RAM zero page $02/$03 must be free as the private count. The sign is tested once on entry and the loop then preserves it, and nonnegative values branch into the shared logical loop at $B550 -- one byte earlier than the male $B551. Clobbers $02/$03 and processor flags. Counts greater than 15 converge to $FFFF for negative values and zero otherwise. Hardware: Touches no hardware: zero-page shifting only. Clobbers: A, X, Y and the processor flags; writes RAM:shared_scratch_02_hi, RAM:shared_scratch_02_lo, $01,X, $00,X.

Female edition-shifted occupant; behavior matches the male helper one byte later.
Standalone logical-right-shift entry for a caller-owned unsigned 16-bit value. Input: A=count low byte, X=count high byte, Y=direct-page address of the value at Y/Y+1. LSR of the high byte followed by ROR of the low byte performs each round. The signed helper at $B528 branches into the internal loop at $B550 for nonnegative values. Output: shifted value in place; A=0, X=0, Y=1. Assumptions: Valid only while the female overlay is the live occupant of $8466-$CC69. Y must be a zero-page address of a 16-bit value at Y and Y+1 (so $FE or below), RAM zero page $02/$03 must be free as the private count, and A/X supply the count. Its loop at $B550 is shared with the signed helper at $B528, so relocating either breaks both; no active caller currently targets this standalone entry. Clobbers $02/$03 and flags. No recorded active caller currently targets this standalone entry. Hardware: Touches no hardware: zero-page shifting only. Clobbers: A, X and the processor flags; writes RAM:shared_scratch_02_lo, RAM:shared_scratch_02_hi.
